summary: Defines an ENUM NAPTR record type for Internet fax (IFax) service. DNS returns the email address of the target IFax system, so a sender can use a telephone number to reach it instead of needing to know the address in advance. It is a standards-track document.

plainLanguage.summary: You know your friend's phone number but not their mailbox. This memo lets a directory turn the phone number into the right email address so your fax finds them.

questions: send fax using phone number via dns
subtitle: Registers the E2U+ifax ENUM service so a telephone number can resolve to an email address for fax.

tldr.problem: Email-based fax (IFax) needs the recipient's email address, which a sender may not know even when they know the telephone number.
tldr.mechanism: An IFax client makes an ENUM DNS query with the telephone number, and the returned NAPTR record gives a mailto: email address for the target system.
tldr.outcome: A sender can reach an IFax system by phone number. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists RFC 6118 as updating it.

today: RFC 4143 is a Proposed Standard, and RFC 6118 is listed as updating it.

sections.title: What the Service Does
sections.content:
IFax is facsimile using Internet mail. An IFax client makes an ENUM DNS query using the target system's telephone number, and the returned NAPTR record specifies an email address for reaching the target.

That address is then used with Simple Mode of Facsimile using Internet Mail (RFC 3965), Extended Facsimile using Internet Mail (RFC 2532), or the Full Mode Fax Profile for Internet Mail (RFC 4142).
sections.plainLanguage: You ask the directory for a phone number and it answers with an email address that your fax is sent to.

sections.title: The Registration
sections.content:
The service name is E2U+ifax, with type ifax, subtype mailto and URI scheme mailto. The scheme is mailto because facsimile is a profile of standard Internet mail and uses standard Internet mail addressing.

Intended usage is COMMON. The authors are Kiyoshi Toyoda and Dave Crocker, and the registration is made according to the terms of RFC 3761.
sections.plainLanguage: The form says the service is about fax, and the answer is an ordinary email address.

sections.title: An Example Record
sections.content: The RFC gives an example NAPTR record for the number's reversed-digit domain under e164.arpa. The record uses order and preference 10 and 10, flag u, service E2U+ifax:mailto, and a rewrite rule that returns mailto:toyo@example.com.
sections.plainLanguage: The sample entry shows a number turning into the address toyo@example.com.

sections.title: Privacy and Security
sections.content:
DNS is a globally distributed database, so anything stored in it is visible to anyone anonymously. Publishing a telephone number with an IFax service can expose it to harvesting and to "junk faxes". Unlike email, where users can have "sacrificial" addresses, a user normally has a single E.164 number, so that trick is not available.

As a principle, the data subject MUST give explicit informed consent to data being published in ENUM. The security sections of RFC 3965, RFC 2532 and the ENUM specification also apply.
sections.plainLanguage: Anyone can read the directory, so a number listed there might get junk faxes. People must say yes before they are listed.
